questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify the correct statements from the following:
(i) $\mathrm{Ti}(\mathrm{IV})$ is more stable than Ti (III) and Ti (II)
(ii) Among 3d-series elements (from $Z=22$ to 29) only copper has positive reduction potential ( $\mathrmM^{2+} / \mathrm{M}$ )
(iii) Both Sc and Zn exhibit +1 oxidation state
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Ti}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{ d}^2 4 \mathrm{ s}^2 \\
& \mathrm{Ti}^{3+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{ d}^1 4 \mathrm{ s}^0 \\
& \mathrm{Ti}^{4+}=[\mathrm{Ar}] 3 \mathrm{ d}^{{}^{\circ}} 4 \mathrm{ s}^0
\end{aligned}$
As $\mathrm{Ti}^{4+}$ have vacant d-orbital and it acquires nearest noble gas configuration so it is more stable as compare to $\mathrm{Ti}^{3+}$ which does not have vacant d -orbitals.
$\mathrm{Cu}^{2+} / \mathrm{Cu}=0.34$ have exceptionally positive reduction potential.
Sc show oxidation state +2 and +3 and Zn show +2 .
So only (i) and (ii) are correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Choose the correct statement from the following with reference to inert pair effect
options: $\mathrm{Sn}^{+4}$ is reducing agent but $\mathrm{Pb}^{+4}$ is an oxidizing agent
$\mathrm{Sn}^{+4}$ is an oxidizing agent but $\mathrm{Pb}^{+2}$ is a reducing agent
$\mathrm{Sn}^{+2}$ is reducing agent but $\mathrm{Pb}^{+4}$ is an oxidizing agent
$\mathrm{Sn}^{+2}$ is an oxidizing agent but $\mathrm{Pb}^{+4}$ is a reducing agent
questions.solution:
The inert pair effect results in the stabilization of an oxidation state, two units less than the common group oxidation state.
The stability of the oxidation state, two units less than the group oxidation state increases down the group.
Thus, $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$ is much more stable than $\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}$ because of which $\mathrm{Pb}^{4+}$ acts as an oxidizing agent and itself gets reduced to $\mathrm{Pb}^{2+}$.
$\mathrm{Sn}^{2+}$ acts as a reducing agent and gets oxidized to $\mathrm{Sn}^{4+}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The number f-electrons in +3 oxidation state of gadolinium $(Z=64)$ is $x$ and in +2 oxidation state of Ytterbium $(\mathrm{Z}=70)$ is $\mathrm{y}$. The sum of $\mathrm{x}$ and $\mathrm{y}$ is
questions.solution:
The outer electronic configuration for $\mathrm{Gd}$ and $\mathrm{Yb}$ are:-
$\begin{aligned}
& \mathrm{Gd}=4 f^7 5 \mathrm{ d}^1 6 \mathrm{ s}^2 \\
& \mathrm{Yb}=4 f^{14} 6 \mathrm{ s}^2
\end{aligned}$
Thus, $\mathrm{Gd}^{3+}=4 f^7$ and $\mathrm{yb}^{2+}=4 f^{14}$
Thus, x=7 and $y=14\Rightarrow x+y=7+14=21$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify all the correct statements for Lanthanide contraction.
(A) The covalent properties of the Lanthanide metal hydroxides increases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(B) The chemical reactivity decreases from $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$.
(C) $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$
(D) Zr and Hf have about the same radius.
(E) Separation of Lanthanides from one another is easy
questions.solution:
The change in ionic radii is Lanthanide series is very small, their chemical properties are small. Thus, the separation of Lanthanide is difficult due to consequence of Lanthanide contraction.
The ionic radii of same positive charge of $\mathrm{La}$ to $\mathrm{Lu}$ decreases. So, the polarizing power towards hydroxyl group increases. Therefore the covalent character increases. Thus, $\mathrm{La}(\mathrm{OH})_3$ is more basic than $\mathrm{Lu}(\mathrm{OH})_3$. $\mathrm{Zr}$ and $\mathrm{Hf}$ have the almost same radius as the electrons in the elements after $\mathrm{Zr}$ are added into the deep seated $4 \mathrm{f}$ orbitals which do not take part in the chemical reaction.

Assertion is false but Reason is true
questions.solution: The transition metals (with the exception of $Zn, Cd\text{and}Hg$) are very much hard and have low volatility. Their melting and boiling points are high.The high melting points of these metals are attributed to the involvement of greater number of electrons from $( n - 1 ) d$ in addition to the $ns$ electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding. In any row the melting points of these metals rise to a maximum at $d^{5}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The most basic hydroxide among the following is
questions.solution:
Basicity is a measure of the ease at which an atom will lose electron. For the lanthanides,& the basicity decreases as the atomic number increases.

The order of the basicity for the lanthanides are${La}^{3 +} > {Ce}^{3 +} > {Pr}^{3 +} > {Nd}^{3 +} > {Pm}^{3 +} > {Sm}^{3 +} > {Eu}^{3 +} > {Gd}^{3 +} > {Tb}^{3 +} > {Dy}^{3 +} > {Ho}^{3 +} > {Er}^{3 +} > {Tm}^{3 +} > {Yb}^{3 +} > {Lu}^{3 +}$

and also ${Ce}^{+ 4}$ is less& stable than ${Ce}^{+ 3}$ and thus it will readily accept $e^{-}$ convert into ${Ce}^{+ 3}$ and so it will less basic than ${Ce}^{+ 3}$.

Hence, from all above observations it can be concluded that $Ce{( OH )}_{3}$is most basic among all given options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation state of $Cr$ in ${CrO}_{5}$ is
questions.solution:
In ${CrO}_{5}$, one oxygen is attached to $Cr$ through the double bond. It has oxidation number $- 2$. Four oxygen atoms are attached to $Cr$ atom through a single bond. Each of these oxygen atoms possess oxidation number $- 1$.

Let $x$ be the oxidation number of chromium. The net charge on ${CrO}_{5}$ is zero.

Hence,&

$x - 2 + 4\left(- 1\right) = 0x = + 6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The main products formed when copper metal is reacted with concentrated ${HNO}_{3}$ are
questions.solution:
Copper is a transition element. ${HNO}_{3}$ is nitric acid. When the concentrated nitric acid reacts with the copper metal then it formed the copper nitrate and nitrogen dioxide gas. So, the nitric acid will decompose into the nitrogen dioxide gas and copper nitrate.

Reaction :-

$Cu + Conc. {HNO}_{3} \to Cu\left({NO}_{3}\right)^{2} + {NO}_{2}$

Hence, the main products formed when copper metal is reacted with concentrated ${HNO}_{3}$ are $Cu\left({NO}_{3}\right)^{2}; {NO}_{2}$.
